BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r7.claim: Past-tense labels for disbelievers could despairingly include those who later repent; God therefore tells the Prophet to invite them to stop, promising forgiveness and erasure of past sins.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r7.anchor: أقبل توبة من تاب منهم بمجرد انتهائه عن حاله

BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r8.claim: The passive wording of forgiveness emphasizes the benefit itself: past sins are erased in both substance and trace, with no punishment or reproach.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r8.anchor: بناه للمفعول لأن النافع نفس الغفران وهو محو الذنب

BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r9.claim: If they persist and resume hostilities, the precedent of earlier peoples has already run its course, as shown by reports of the past and what was witnessed at Badr.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p216/r9.anchor: أي وجدت وانقضت ونفذت فلا مرد لها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r3.claim: God commands the Prophet to convey the promise that ending disbelief brings forgiveness for the past; the message need not use these exact words.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r3.anchor: أمر من الله عز وجل لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقول للكفار هذا المعنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r4.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r4.claim: Al-Kisa'i says Ibn Masud's codex reads يغفر لكم; Ibn Atiyya argues that if this were the wording, conveying the message would require those exact words.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r4.anchor: ذكر الكسائي أنه في مصحف ابن مسعود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r5.claim: If they desist means desist from disbelief, since forgiveness of what preceded follows only when disbelief is abandoned.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r5.anchor: يريد به عن الكفر ولا بد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r6.claim: If they return means return to fighting: absolute عاد يعود denotes resuming a former state one left, and fighting is the only such state in this passage; returning to disbelief is impossible because they remain in it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r6.anchor: ولا يصح أن يتأول وإن يعودوا إلى الكفر لأنهم لم ينفصلوا عنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r7.claim: In Arabic عاد can instead take a predicate and mean صار, 'became'; in that use it does not mean returning to a former state and cannot stand without its predicate, as Abu al-Salt's verse illustrates.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r7.anchor: لأنها قد تجيء في كلام العرب داخلة على الابتداء والخبر بمنزلة صار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r8.claim: The past custom of earlier peoples is a threat recalling nations destroyed when they opposed their prophets and those killed at Badr by Islam's sword; the audience has seen or heard what happened.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p527/r8.anchor: عبارة بجمع الوعيد والتهديد والتمثيل بمن هلك من الأمم في سالف الدهر

TABATABAI:8:37-39/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:37-39/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:37-39/r3.claim: Intihāʾ means stopping because of a prohibition, salaf means what came before, and sunnah means a path or practice; the Prophet is to invite them to stop fighting so earlier crimes may be forgiven.
TABATABAI:8:37-39/r3.anchor: الانتهاء الإقلاع عن الشيء لأجل النهي، والسلوف التقدم، والسنة هي الطريقة والسيرة

TABATABAI:8:37-39/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:8:37-39/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:8:37-39/r4.claim: If they persist, God’s established precedent brings destruction and loss, as happened to their predecessors.
TABATABAI:8:37-39/r4.anchor: فقد مضت سنة الله في الأولين منهم بالإهلاك والإبادة وخسران السعي

THALABI:v4p356/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p356/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد أحمد بن محمد الزيدي
THALABI:v4p356/r1.claim: A poem says a person who admits and abandons wrongdoing deserves pardon, citing God’s promise to forgive those who desist.
THALABI:v4p356/r1.anchor: أبو سعيد أحمد بن محمد الزيدي: يستوجب العفو الفتى إذا اعترف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r6.claim: The command to unbelievers is addressed to Abū Sufyān and his companions: if they stop associating partners and fighting believers, past sins will be forgiven.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r7.claim: A former enemy who becomes Muslim is like one newly born; if they resume fighting, God's established pattern is to give messengers and believers victory.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:8:36-38/r7.anchor: لأن الحربي إذا أسلم عاد كمثله يوم ولدته أمه

ELMALILI:8:36-38/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:36-38/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:36-38/r6.claim: If the unbelievers stop fighting and submit to the truth, their past sins will be forgiven; if they return to war, they should expect the same fate as earlier peoples who opposed their prophets, with Badr as a sufficient example.
ELMALILI:8:36-38/r6.anchor: bulundukları hâli bırakıp hakka teslîm-i nefs ederlerse

ELMALILI:8:36-38/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:8:36-38/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:8:36-38/r7.claim: God's decree that He and His messengers will prevail, and that righteous servants inherit the earth, supports the warning if unbelievers return to hostility.
ELMALILI:8:36-38/r7.anchor: Bunlar misâl-i kâfîdir. Binâen‘aleyh dönüp onların yolunu tutarlar, onların âdetine sülûk ederlerse

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p35.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p35.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p35.claim: The Quraysh should change course and accept the Prophet's message, or remember the fate of earlier peoples who denied their messengers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p35.anchor: it is better if they change their ways and accept the Prophet’s message; otherwise, they should remember

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.claim: The Quraysh are invited to avert doom by stopping their hostility, repenting, reforming, and accepting the Prophet; God will forgive their past and not punish them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.anchor: they should abstain from this attitude, repent, mend their ways and accept the message of the Prophet

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.claim: The warning immediately follows the invitation: if the Quraysh repeat their hostility, the divine precedent for earlier peoples applies to them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p44.anchor: The words “and if they repeat it, then the practice of God for the previous people has passed” is a sentence of warning right after they were exhorted

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p45.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p45.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p45.claim: When a messenger has conclusively delivered the truth, continued disbelief brings certain destruction, by calamity or the believers’ sword.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p45.anchor: a nation to whom God’s sends a messenger is conclusively delivered the truth by Him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p45.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p45.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p45.claim: A messenger is the final means of conclusive communication, so the condemned nation receives no further respite.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anfal-08:p45.anchor: A messenger is the greatest, in fact, the final means of conclusive communication of the truth to its nation.

STUDYQURAN:8:38/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r1.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r1.claim: Some commentators read desisting as ending enmity and hostility and embracing Islam.
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r1.anchor: According to some commentators, this verse means that the disbelievers should stop their enmity and hostility and embrace Islam

STUDYQURAN:8:38/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r2.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r2.claim: The final clause refers to God's established practice of destroying persistently corrupt and evil peoples.
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r2.anchor: The last clause refers to God’s wont of destroying persistently corrupt and evil peoples

STUDYQURAN:8:38/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r3.claim: Wont can describe both what people do and what they undergo.
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r3.anchor: Wont can also refer to both what people do and what they undergo

STUDYQURAN:8:38/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r4.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r4.claim: A hadith states that submission and repentance each cut off what came before.
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r4.anchor: In a ḥadīth the Prophet said

STUDYQURAN:8:38/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r5.claim: The verse does not explicitly require conversion to Islam; forgiveness can mean ending hostilities and resolving grievances.
STUDYQURAN:8:38/r5.anchor: this verse says nothing explicitly about the disbelievers becoming Muslims, and “forgiveness” can refer to the cessation of hostilities

TAB-FULL:v11p176/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r1.claim: If the Meccan polytheists stop their unbelief and fighting God, His Messenger, and believers, and repent into faith, their prior sins are forgiven through faith and repentance.
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r1.anchor: إن ينتهوا عما هم عليه مقيمون من كفرهم بالله ورسوله وقتالك وقتال المؤمنين فينيبوا إلى الإيمان

TAB-FULL:v11p176/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r2.claim: If they resume fighting after Badr, God will punish them as He punished earlier peoples who rebelled, denied messengers, and rejected their counsel.
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r2.anchor: فقد مضت سنتي في الأولين منهم ببدر ومن غيرهم من القرون الخالية إذ طغوا وكذبوا رسلي

TAB-FULL:v11p176/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the precedent concerns Quraysh at Badr and other nations before them.
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: " {فقد مضت سنة الأولين}

TAB-FULL:v11p176/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r4.claim: Ibn Isḥāq interprets their return as returning to war against the Prophet and says the earlier precedent is their people killed at Badr.
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r4.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال في قوله

TAB-FULL:v11p176/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v11p176/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says that if they return to fight, the precedent is that of the people of Badr.

TABRISI:8:38-39/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:38-39/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:38-39/r1.claim: Intiha is desisting from something because of a prohibition; sunna and tariqa are synonyms for a way or practice.
TABRISI:8:38-39/r1.anchor: الانتهاء الإقلاع عن الشيء لأجل النهي يقال نهاه عن كذا فانتهى والسنة والطريقة والسيرة نظائر

TABRISI:8:38-39/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:38-39/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:38-39/r2.claim: Salaf means those who came before; tawalli from religion means turning away toward its opposite, while tawalli in religion means turning toward truth and following it.
TABRISI:8:38-39/r2.anchor: والسلوف التقدم والتولي عن الدين الذهاب عنه إلى خلافه والتولي فيه هو الذهاب إلى جهة الحق ومتابعته

TABRISI:8:38-39/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:38-39/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:38-39/r4.claim: God commands the Prophet to invite the unbelievers to repentance and faith.
TABRISI:8:38-39/r4.anchor: ثم أمر سبحانه نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم بدعائهم إلى التوبة والإيمان

TABRISI:8:38-39/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:38-39/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:38-39/r5.claim: If they repent from and desist from their polytheism, their past sins will be forgiven.
TABRISI:8:38-39/r5.anchor: أي يتوبوا عما هم عليه من الشرك ويمتنعوا منه

TABRISI:8:38-39/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:38-39/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:38-39/r6.claim: Another explanation is that if they stop fighting and make peace, their past punishments will be forgiven.
TABRISI:8:38-39/r6.anchor: وقيل: إن ينتهوا عن المحاربة إلى الموادعة يغفر لهم ما قد سلف من المعاقبة

TABRISI:8:38-39/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:38-39/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:38-39/r7.claim: If they return to fighting and persist in disbelief, God's established treatment of their ancestors will apply: believers are supported and enemies humiliated, captured, and enslaved.
TABRISI:8:38-39/r7.anchor: وإن يعودوا إلى القتال وأصروا على الكفر فقد مضت سنة الله في آبائكم وعادته في نصر المؤمنين

TABRISI:8:38-39/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:8:38-39/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:8:38-39/r8.claim: The customary outcome is attributed to those who undergo it, to messengers through whom it is carried out, and to God as its cause.
TABRISI:8:38-39/r8.anchor: وأضاف السنة إليهم لأنها كانت تجري عليهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies those addressed as Abu Sufyan and his companions.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says they must desist from denying Muhammad and from associating partners with God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد عن تكذيبك (¬3) وعن الشرك بالله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says the required desistance is from fighting Muhammad and his companions.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: عن قتال محمد وأصحابه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r4.claim: سلف means to precede or pass; أسلف is to pay in advance, السالفة is the forward neck, and السلافة is the first extracted wine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r4.anchor: السالفة: العنق لتقدمها على البدن، والسلافة من الخمر: أخلصها؛ لتقدمها بالتحلب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says what has passed includes fornication, idolatry, murder, usury, and every other disapproved act.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ما قد سلف: يريد من الزنا والشرك والقتل والربا وكل مكروه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r6.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r6.claim: The third-person yāʾ in ينتهوا suits an instruction to address absent people; using the second-person tāʾ would directly quote the address, as in 3:12.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r6.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: قوله: {إن ينتهوا} بالياء إنما جاز وحسن لأنه أمره بمخاطبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r7.speaker: العلماء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r7.claim: The scholars compare the verse with the hadith Islam erases what came before: a belligerent convert need not make up bodily or financial worship, and prior injuries to life or property are forgiven.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r7.anchor: قال العلماء: وهذه الآية كقوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r8.speaker: العلماء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r8.claim: The scholars say the convert begins his Muslim life as though newly born, without prior debts for acts of worship.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r8.anchor: وهو ساعة إسلامه كيوم ولدته أمه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r9.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r9.claim: Yahya ibn Muadh wittily hopes that just as monotheism erases earlier disbelief, it can erase later sins too.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p148/r9.anchor: وما أظرف ما قال يحيى بن معاذ (¬6) في هذه الآية: إن # توحيدا لم يعجز عن هدم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says this means if they return to denying Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: إلى تكذيبك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi says if they return to fighting Muhammad, the precedent of earlier peoples will apply: God aided His messengers and believers against disbelievers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي: {وإن يعودوا} لقتالك {فقد مضت سنت الأولين} بنصر الله رسله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r3.claim: Qatada says God's established way was to grant victory to messengers over earlier nations and likewise to this community at Badr; he links 58:21 and 37:171.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: مضت السنة من الله في الأولين من الأمم بنصر الله الرسل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r4.claim: Al-Suddi and Ibn Ishaq say the precedent was God's victory for the messengers and believers at Badr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v10p150/r4.anchor: وقال السدي وابن إسحاق: {فقد مضت سنت الأولين} بنصر الله الرسل، والمؤمنين يوم بدر

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r1.claim: The verse answers what happens to the past acts of people from other faiths who harmed believers or committed acts treated as sins in Islam: God forgives their deeds from disbelief when they enter Islam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r1.anchor: Âyet bu soruya cevap veriyor: Allah onların kâfir iken yaptıklarını bağışlayacaktır, İslâm’a girdikleri andan itibaren sabıka kayıtları silinecek

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r2.claim: On conversion, a person's earlier record is erased and a clean page opens.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r2.anchor: İslâm’a girdikleri andan itibaren sabıka kayıtları silinecek, kendileri için beyaz bir sayfa açılacaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r3.speaker: fıkıhçılar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r3.claim: Jurists, reading this verse with related texts and principles, conclude that God forgives His own rights and does not hold a newly guided person accountable for prior sins whose root was disbelief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r3.anchor: Allah kendi haklarını bağışlar, geçmiş günahlarının temeli ve âmili olan inkâr hali ortadan kalktığı için hidâyete ermiş olan kulunu daha önce yaptıklarından sorumlu tutmaz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r4.speaker: fıkıhçılar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r4.claim: Human claims are still made good materially: damages are compensated, wrongfully acquired property returned, and consumed property reimbursed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r4.anchor: Kul haklarına gelince bunların maddî bakımdan telâfisi yoluna gidilir, zararlar tazmin ettirilir, haksız yoldan elde edilen mallar sahiplerine iade edilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r5.speaker: Ebû Bekir İbnü’l-Arabî; İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r5.claim: Some scholars read the verse's general wording to forgive every crime and wrong committed while in disbelief after conversion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r5.anchor: Âyetteki genel ifadeye bakarak inkâr halinde işlenen her suçun, yapılan her kötülüğün müslüman olduktan sonra bağışlanacağını söyleyen âlimler de olmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r6.claim: Erasing sins and worldly liability after guidance strongly encourages people to convert to Islam.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:8:38/r6.anchor: İnkâr halinde işlenmiş suç ve günahların hidâyete erdikten sonra silinmesi ve hidâyeti seçen kimsenin dünyada da bunlardan sorumlu tutulmaması hükmü ihtidâyı teşvik bakımından büyük bir önem taşımaktadır

BURHAN:v2p229/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p229/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p229/r5.claim: Unbelievers are often mentioned in the third person as an expression of turning away from them, while believers are directly addressed with the order to fight.
BURHAN:v2p229/r5.anchor: وكثر الخطاب ب يأيها الذين آمنوا على المواجهة

BURHAN:v3p209/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p209/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p209/r2.claim: If the rejecters return to opposition, what befell earlier peoples will befall them.
BURHAN:v3p209/r2.anchor: وإن يعودوا فقد مضت سنة الأولين

BURHAN:v1p413/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p413/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p413/r1.claim: When sunnah means the retributive fate of earlier nations, as in the Anfal verse, its spelling reflects this concrete action sense, supported by the surrounding warning and fight command.
BURHAN:v1p413/r1.anchor: ويدل عليها أنها من الانتقام قوله قبلها

BURHAN:v1p446/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p446/r3.speaker: الشبلي
BURHAN:v1p446/r3.claim: Al-Shibli calls the promise to forgive prior sins upon conversion the most hopeful: if God admits disbelievers who profess unity and testimony, He will not expel those who enter and remain.
BURHAN:v1p446/r3.anchor: قل للذين كفروا إن ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف

BURHAN:v2p114/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p114/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p114/r1.claim: The section asks about Qur’anic phrases that coincide with metrical poetry, whether a full line, several lines, or a hemistich, while treating such coincidence as distinct from poetry.
BURHAN:v2p114/r1.anchor: فإن قيل فقد وجد فى القرآن ما وافق شعرا موزونا إما بيت تام أو أبيات أو مصراع

BURHAN:v2p114/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p114/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p114/r9.claim: The author adds Qur’anic phrases as examples of metrical coincidence, including night worship, charity, disputing, the flood, Abu Lahab, victory, conversion, and Qarun.

BURHAN:v4p215/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p215/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p215/r1.claim: The conditional إن is the most common use, including the promise that if disbelievers desist they are forgiven.

BURHAN:v2p354/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p354/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p354/r1.claim: Normally a conditional result is warranted by the condition’s actual occurrence: visiting warrants generosity, and gratitude warrants a visit.
BURHAN:v2p354/r1.anchor: الثانية اصل الشرط والجزاء ان يتوفق الثاني على الاول بمعنى ان الشرط

BURHAN:v4p423/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p423/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p423/r1.claim: The apparent conflict between the two forgiveness promises disappears because the verse about Noah’s people addresses a different group from the promise to this community.
BURHAN:v4p423/r1.anchor: فإن الآية التى فيها من قوم نوح والأخرى لهذه الأمة

BURHAN:v4p423/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p423/r2.speaker: الأخفش
BURHAN:v4p423/r2.claim: An objection says partial forgiveness weakens the incentive to believe and conflicts with Islam erasing earlier sins, supporting al-Akhfash’s view that min is extra.
BURHAN:v4p423/r2.anchor: فكيف يحسن التبعيض فيها مع إن الإسلام يجب ما قبله فيصح قول الأخفش

BURHAN:v4p423/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p423/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p423/r4.claim: Another answer notes that conversion does not erase obligations for wrongs against other people, so some sins remain for a convert.
BURHAN:v4p423/r4.anchor: والثاني إن الكافر إذا آمن فقد بقي عليه ذنوب وهي مظالم العباد

BURHAN:v4p423/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p423/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p423/r5.claim: Because your sins can include past and future acts, min restricts the promise to past sins and avoids implying that faith alone pardons future disobedience.
BURHAN:v4p423/r5.anchor: فقيل من لتفيد إن المغفور الماضي وعدم إطماعهم في غفران المستقبل

BURHAN:v4p423/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p423/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p423/r6.claim: Min may instead mark the starting point, which suits the explicit phrase what has gone before; Sibawayh preserves its partitive force by positing an omitted object, some of your sins.
BURHAN:v4p423/r6.anchor: وقيل إنها لابتداء الغاية وهو حسن

BURHAN:v4p423/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p423/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p423/r7.claim: An unnamed reading takes the ellipsis as magnifying the forgiveness: it covers a matter so tremendous that revealing its full nature would make people deem it immense.
BURHAN:v4p423/r7.anchor: وقيل بل الحذف للتفخيم والتقدير يغفر لكم من ذنوبكم ما لو كشف لكم عن كنهه لاستعظمتم ذلك

BURHAN:v4p423/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p423/r8.speaker: الصفار
BURHAN:v4p423/r8.claim: Al-Saffar keeps min partitive: since forgive takes two objects, al-Akhfash makes the stated sins the second and treats min as extra, while the author’s group supplies an omitted object represented by the phrase.
BURHAN:v4p423/r8.anchor: وقال الصفار من للتبعيض على بابها وذلك ان غفر تتعدى لمفعولين أحدهما باللام

ITQAN:v2p449#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p449#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p449#3/r1.claim: إن with kasra and no shadda is conditional in “if they desist, they will be forgiven.”

ITQAN:v2p449#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p449#3/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p449#3/r2.claim: When conditional إن is followed by لم, لم governs the jussive; when followed by لا, إن governs it, because لم binds its verb while إن permits an intervening element and لا does not govern jussive mood.
ITQAN:v2p449#3/r2.anchor: وإذا دخلت على لم فالجزم بلم لا بها لنحو

ITQAN:v3p172/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p172/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p172/r2.claim: In “if they return, the precedent of the ancients has passed,” the omitted consequence is that the same fate will befall them.

ITQAN:v1p297/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p297/r2.speaker: تاج الدين ابن السبكي
ITQAN:v1p297/r2.claim: Ibn al-Subki attributes to Abu Mansur al-Baghdadi a poem urging a sinner to repent and quoting the promise that if disbelievers desist, their past will be forgiven; some considered such borrowing improper, while the author's stature was cited in its defense.
ITQAN:v1p297/r2.anchor: وذكر الشيخ تاج الدين بن السبكي في طبقاته في ترجمة الإمام أبي منصور

ITQAN:v1p297/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p297/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p297/r3.claim: The author says al-Baghdadi's couplet is not technically iqtibās because it explicitly attributes the wording to God's speech, which the prior definition excludes.
ITQAN:v1p297/r3.anchor: قلت ليس هذان البيتان من الاقتباس لتصريحه بقول الله وقد قدمنا أن ذلك خارج عنه

ITQAN:v1p297/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p297/r4.speaker: بهاء الدين ابن السبكي
ITQAN:v1p297/r4.claim: Baha al-Din says scrupulous piety means avoiding all such borrowing and keeping the words of God and His Messenger above it.
ITQAN:v1p297/r4.anchor: وأما أخوه الشيخ بهاء الدين فقال في عروس الأفراح الورع اجتناب ذلك كله وأن ينزه عن مثله كلام الله ورسوله

ITQAN:v1p297/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p297/r7.speaker: النخعي
ITQAN:v1p297/r7.claim: Al-Nawawi notes a disagreement over using Qurʾanic recitation to mean ordinary speech; al-Nakhaʿi reportedly disliked interpreting Qurʾan for a worldly situation that arose.
ITQAN:v1p297/r7.anchor: روى النخعي أنه كان يكره أن يتأول القرآن لشيء يعرض من أمر الدنيا

ITQAN:v4p428/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p428/r6.speaker: الشبلي
ITQAN:v4p428/r6.claim: Al-Shibli says that if God opens the door to an unbeliever who embraces monotheism and testimony, He surely will not cast out those who enter and remain within it.
ITQAN:v4p428/r6.anchor: قال الشبلي إذا كان الله أذن للكافر بدخول الباب إذا أتى بالتوحيد والشهادة أفتراه يخرج الداخل فيها والمقيم عليها

ITQAN:v3p72/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p72/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p72/r1.claim: Apparent conflicts between Qur’anic passages are not real contradictions; as with apparently conflicting hadith, they require explanation, a task Ibn Abbas also addressed.
ITQAN:v3p72/r1.anchor: والمراد به ما يوهم التعارض بين الآيات وكلامه تعالى منزه عن ذلك

ITQAN:v3p185/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p185/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p185/r5.claim: The strongest explanation is that prophetic stories recur to warn of the destruction of those who deny messengers; repeated denials of Muhammad prompted repeated warnings, while Joseph’s story serves another purpose.
ITQAN:v3p185/r5.anchor: وجواب خامس وهو أقوى ما يجاب به أن قصص الأنبياء إنما كررت لأن المقصود بها إفادة إهلاك من كذبوا رسلهم

SAMIN-DURR:8:38/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:38/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:38/r1.claim: The lām may mark transmission: the Prophet is told to convey the statement's meaning to the unbelievers, whether or not in these exact words.
SAMIN-DURR:8:38/r1.anchor: في هذه اللام الوجهان المشهوران: إما التبليغ، أمر أن يبلغهم معنى هذه الجملة المحكية بالقول

SAMIN-DURR:8:38/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:38/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:8:38/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the lām as causal and rejects transmission: say this for their sake; if addressed directly, the wording would be إن تنتهوا يغفر لكم, as in Ibn Masʿūd's reading, and compare 46:11.
SAMIN-DURR:8:38/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنها للتعليل وبه قال الزمخشري ومنع أن تكون للتبليغ فقال:

SAMIN-DURR:8:38/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:8:38/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:8:38/r3.claim: A variant reads يغفر in the active voice, with its subject referring to God.
SAMIN-DURR:8:38/r3.anchor: وقرئ " يغفر " مبنيا للفاعل، وهو ضمير يعود على الله تعالى.

ASAD-NOTES:8:38#n37/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:38#n37/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:8:38#n37/r1.claim: Desisting means abandoning efforts to turn others from God's path and stopping the war against believers.
ASAD-NOTES:8:38#n37/r1.anchor: from their endeavour to turn others away from the path of God and from waging war against the believers

ASAD-NOTES:8:38#n38/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:8:38#n38/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:8:38#n38/r1.claim: The phrase means the example of earlier peoples; it alludes to disasters that have overtaken and will overtake those who persistently deny moral truths.
ASAD-NOTES:8:38#n38/r1.anchor: the example (sunnah) of the people of old times has already come to pass

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1074/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1074/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1074/r1.claim: He describes mercy as the through-line of Maryam and notes guidance occurs 17 times in Al-A'raf, 8 in Al-Isra, and 6 in Al-Kahf, linking the greater frequency to an added yāʾ.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1074/r1.anchor: سورة مريم فيها الرحمة من أولها إلى آخرها

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: When a name ending in tāʾ marbūṭa is treated after truncation as a name without it, عرقوة and قمحدوة yield عرقى and قمحدى.

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: The same truncation analysis gives يا رعى from رعوم and يا قطا from قطوان.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: وكذلك إن رخمت رعوم وجعلته بهذه المنزلة قلت يا رعى

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: طفاوة becomes يا طفاء when the remainder is treated as a name without tāʾ, because the language has no noun with that final pattern.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: يا طفاء أقبل من قبل أنه ليس في الكلام اسم هكذا

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: If the remaining wāw is not made an inflectional ending, it stays unchanged after truncating طفاوة: يا طفاو.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: فهي على حالها قبل أن تحذف الهاء

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: Treating the remainder as a noun without tāʾ is less common; speakers more often preserve its form because case endings elsewhere change.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: واعلم أن ما يجعل بمنزلة اسم

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: The truncation يا معا from معاوية is supported by al-ʿAjjāj's verse, showing that this treatment is native Arabic.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: قد حملهم ذلك على أن رخموه

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: حيوة becomes يا حيو; in the nominative its wāw remains by the original pattern غزو, so the change is not obligatory.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: وتقول في حيوة يا حيو أقبل

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: One may not drop tāʾ and treat the remainder as masculine for an ordinary feminine noun, since that would confuse gender; the exception is a dominant proper name.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: واعلم أنه لا يجوز أن تحذف الهاء وتجعل البقية

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: Truncation of names not ending in tāʾ is less common because it removes both tanwin and an inherent final consonant, though it is permitted.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: أن لا يحذف منها أكثر لأنهم كرهوا أن يخلوا بها

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: Names such as حارث, مالك, and عامر are especially often shortened because they are frequent personal names and common in poetry; several poets attest them.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: وليس الحذف لشئ من هذه الأسماء ألزم منه لحارث ومالك وعامر

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: Any proper name may be shortened in address; examples include يزيد as يزى, ليلى as ليل, and لميس as لمى.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: وكل اسم خاص رخمته في النداء

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's verse uses طريف بن مال for طريف بن مالك, showing a name without tāʾ may also be shortened in poetry.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: طريف بن مال ليلة الجوع والخصر

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: The text cites a line attributed to Ṭarafa as a constructed example by an ʿĀbidī poet, with سعد shortened from أسعد.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: مصنوع على طرفة وهو لبعض العباديين

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: Sībawayh reports al-Khalīl's rule that names are shortened from five letters to four and four to three, with three-letter names as the lower limit.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: وكان غاية التخفيف عندهم لأنه أخف شئ

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: Only dominant proper names without tāʾ are normally shortened, since they are frequent enough to undergo deletion even outside address, as in زيد بن عمرو.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: ليس من اسم لا تكون في آخره هاء

SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.claim: يا صاح for صاحب is an exceptional shortening justified by frequent use, like the conventional reductions لم أبل, لم يك, and لا أدر.
SIBAWAYH:وإنلمتجعلهبمنزلةاسمليسفيهالهاءل.anchor: إلا أنهم قد قالوا يا صاح وهم يريدون يا صاحب

IBNHISHAM:v1p671#3/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p671#3/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p671#3/r2.claim: If they resume war after the call to desist, the precedent of earlier peoples means those unbelievers killed at Badr.
IBNHISHAM:v1p671#3/r2.anchor: أي من قتل منهم يوم بدر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r1.claim: After describing the disbelievers' punishment, God offers them a way out: if they abandon disbelief and believe, their past sins are forgiven; disbelief is what they must leave.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r1.anchor: تلطف بهم وأنهم إذا انتهوا عن الكفر وآمنوا غفرت لهم ذنوبهم السالفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r2.claim: The lām in li-lladhīna is for conveying a message: the Prophet is ordered to tell them the clause's meaning, whether in its wording or another wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r2.anchor: واللام في للذين الظاهر أنها للتبليغ وأنه أمر أن يقول لهم هذا المعنى الذي تضمنته ألفاظ الجملة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the lām as causal, “for their sake”; direct address would instead say “if you desist, We forgive you,” as in Ibn Masʿūd's reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r3.anchor: وجعل الزمخشري اللام لام العلة، فقال: أي قل لأجلهم هذا القول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r4.claim: A reading has yaghfir in the active voice, with God as its subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r4.anchor: وقرىء يغفر مبنيا للفاعل والضمير لله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r5.claim: “Return” requires coming back to something left; because they never left disbelief, it means returning to what they could leave, namely fighting the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r5.anchor: العود يقتضي الرجوع إلى شيء سابق ولا يكون الكفر لأنهم لم ينفصلوا عنه فالمعنى عودهم إلى ما أمكن انفصالهم منه وهو قتال رسول الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r6.claim: Another interpretation is that they return to apostasy after having entered Islam; Abū Ḥanīfa explained the verse this way.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r6.anchor: وقيل وإن يعودوا إلى الارتداد بعد الإسلام، وبه فسر أبو حنيفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r7.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa uses the verse to argue that an apostate who returns to Islam need not make up worship omitted before or during apostasy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r7.anchor: واحتج بالآية على أن المرتد إذا أسلم فلا يلزمه قضاء العبادات المتروكة في حال الردة وقبلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r8.claim: There is consensus that conversion by a non-Muslim combatant removes outstanding liabilities; a protected non-Muslim who converts must still repay human claims, but not God's claims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r8.anchor: وأجمعوا على أن الحربي إذا أسلم لم تبق عليه تبعة وأما إذا أسلم الذمي فيلزمه قضاء حقوق الآدميين لا حقوق الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r9.claim: The verse's general address to disbelievers includes the zindīq: Abū Ḥanīfa and al-Shāfiʿī accept his repentance, while Mālik does not.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r9.anchor: والظاهر دخول الزنديق في عموم قوله قل للذين كفروا فتقبل توبته وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة والشافعي وقال مالك لا تقبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r10.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r10.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh al-Rāzī says that if monotheism can erase earlier disbelief, it can certainly erase later sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r10.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ الرازي: التوحيد لا يعجز عن هدم ما قبله من كفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r11.claim: The conditional answer is not simply “the precedent of the ancients has passed”; that phrase signals an omitted threat that God will punish and destroy them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r11.anchor: وجواب الشرط قالوا: فقد مضت سنت الأولين، ولا يصح ذلك على ظاهره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r12.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r12.claim: The precedent may be the destruction of those punished at Badr or of earlier peoples who conspired against their prophets; Badr is the stronger warning because it was recent and witnessed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r12.anchor: ويحتمل سنت الأولين أن يراد بها سنة الذين حاق بهم مكرهم يوم بدر وسنة الذين تحزبوا على أنبيائهم فدمروا فليتوقعوا مثل ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r13.speaker: ابن إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r13.claim: Al-Suddī and Ibn Isḥāq support the interpretation that the threat recalls Badr and earlier destroyed nations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r13.anchor: وتخويفهم بقصة بدر أشد إذ هي قريبة معاينة لهم وعليها نص السدي وابن إسحاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r14.claim: Alternatively, “the precedent of the ancients” refers to Badr's earlier participants and past nations: the audience saw Badr's story and heard what befell them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p318/r14.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد بقوله سنت الأولين من تقدم من أهل بدر والأمم السالفة والمعنى فقد عاينتم قصة بدر وسمعتم ما حل بهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r1.claim: The disbelievers addressed are the familiar group of Abu Sufyan and his companions.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r1.anchor: أي المعهودين وهم أبو سفيان وأصحابه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r2.speaker: جمع
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r2.claim: A group takes the lām as causal: the Prophet is told to say this for the disbelievers' benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r2.anchor: واللام عند جمع للتعليل أي قل لأجلهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the lām as transmission: the Prophet must convey the meaning contained in the quoted sentence, whether or not he uses its exact wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r3.anchor: وقال أبو حيان : الظاهر أن اللام للتبليغ وأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أمر أن يقول هذا المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r4.claim: If they stop opposing the Messenger by entering Islam, their previous sins are forgiven, including hostility and spending to support misguidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r4.anchor: عما هم فيه من معاداة الرسول صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r5.claim: Ibn Mas'ud reads the clause in the second person, 'if you desist, you will be forgiven'; on this reading the lām is necessarily for conveying the message.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r5.anchor: وأما على قراءة ابن مسعود ( إن تنتهوا يغفر لكم ( بالخطاب فلا خلاف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r6.claim: A passive reading, 'it will be forgiven for them,' makes the pronoun refer to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206/r6.anchor: وقريء ( بغفر لهم ) على أن الضمير لله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r1.claim: The precedent is God's recurring treatment of those who conspire against prophets: He supports believers against them, defeats them, and destroys them.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r1.anchor: عادة الله تعالى الجارية في الذين تحزبوا على الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام من نصر المؤمنين عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r2.claim: The precedent is attributed to earlier peoples by association, as in 'a precedent of those We sent' though it is God's precedent carried out through the messengers; al-Alusi cites 17:77 as the parallel.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r2.anchor: ونظير ذلك قوله سبحانه : ( سنة من قد أرسلنا ) فأضاف السنة إلى المرسلين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r3.claim: Some identify the earlier peoples specifically with those whose plotting rebounded on them at Badr; al-Alusi prefers the general interpretation because a sunnah conventionally recurs, even though a habit may be established once.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r3.anchor: وبعضهم فسره بذلك ولعل الأول أولى لعمومه ولأن السنة تقتضي التكرر في العرف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r4.claim: The clause supplies the consequence elliptically: if they return, God will exact vengeance or give the believers victory, as al-Bahr explains.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r4.anchor: والجملة على ما في البحر دليل الجواب والتقدير إن يعودوا انتقمنا منهم أو نصرنا المؤمنين عليهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r5.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r5.claim: Others read the disbelievers generally: abandoning disbelief and becoming Muslim erases prior disbelief and sins, while apostasy back to disbelief restores God's domination over them.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r5.anchor: وذهب غير واحد إلى أن المراد بالذين كفروا الكفار مطلقا والآية حث على الإيمان وترغيب فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r6.claim: The verse is cited for Islam erasing what preceded it, so a convert need not make up missed prayer, zakat, or fasting, or compensate for property or life lost before conversion.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r6.anchor: واستدل بالآية على أن الإسلام يجب ما قبله وأن الكافر إذا أسلم لا يخاطب بقضاء ما فاته من صلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r7.speaker: المالكية
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r7.claim: The Malikis extend this rule to a repentant apostate and cite the verse to cancel pre-Islamic jizya owed by a dhimmi who converts.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r7.anchor: وأجرى المالكية ذلك كله في المرتد إذا تاب لعموم الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r8.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits through Ibn Wahb that Malik said a disbeliever who converts is not held accountable for anything done during disbelief, citing this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم من طريق ابن وهب عن مالك قال : لا يؤاخذ الكافر بشيء صنعه في كفره إذا أسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r9.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r9.claim: One view says a converted combatant disbeliever has no outstanding liability, while a protected non-Muslim owes no divine duties but remains liable for human claims.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r9.anchor: قال بعض : إن الحربي إذا أسلم لم تبق عليه تبعة أصلا وأما الذمي فلا يلزمه قضاء حقوق الله

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa is reported to treat a repentant apostate like the Malikis, clearing prior liabilities; some even attribute to him that lifelong sin followed by apostasy and return leaves no sin, an attribution al-Alusi calls highly strange.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r10.anchor: ونسب إلى الإمام أبي حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه أن مذهبه في المرتد كمذهب المالكية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r11.claim: A report in Ibn Abd al-Haqq's Quran-law work says Abu Hanifa and Malik preserve human claims against the apostate but clear claims belonging to God; al-Shafi'i requires all claims to be discharged.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r11.anchor: كما في كتاب أحكام القرآن لابن عبد الحق وخالفهما الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه وقال : يلزمه جميع الحقوق

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r12.speaker: شمس الأئمة الحلواني
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r12.claim: Al-Halwani says an apostate returning to Islam must make up prayers and fasts he deliberately missed while Muslim; the apostasy does not erase those deliberate omissions.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r12.anchor: قال شمس الأئمة الحلواني : عليه قضاء ما ترك الصلاة والصيام معصية تبقى بعد الردة

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r13.claim: Al-Alusi cites al-Khaniyya's detailed rulings to show that the formula 'human rights remain, divine rights lapse' is not absolute for apostates.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r13.anchor: ومنه يعلم أن قولهم المرتد يلزمه حقوق العباد دون حقوق الله تعالى ليس على إطلاقه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r14.speaker: قاضيخان
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r14.claim: Al-Khaniyya distinguishes where property, retaliation, or defamation claims arose: after apostasy in enemy territory and flight, they are waived on return, but claims arising before that remain enforceable.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r14.anchor: مسلم أصاب مالا أو شيئا يجب به القصاص أو حد قذف ثم ارتد أو أصاب ذلك وهو مرتد في دار الإسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r15.speaker: قاضيخان
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r15.claim: For divine limits committed before or after apostasy and flight, Al-Khaniyya generally waives punishment on return, except stolen property and specified homicide or road-banditry compensation, whose liability depends on when the act occurred.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r15.anchor: فكل ذلك يكون موضوعا عنه إلا أنه يضمن المال في السرقة وإذا أصاب دما في الطريق كان عليه القصاص

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r16.speaker: قاضيخان
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r16.claim: For drinking, apostasy before conversion prevents a new limit from being imposed; if the offense occurs while imprisoned, wine penalties are treated differently from other divine limits and depend on whether the ruler already has custody.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r16.anchor: وإن وجب على المسلم حد الشرب ثم ارتد ثم أسلم قبل اللحوق بدار الحرب فإنه لا يؤاخذ بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r17.claim: Al-Alusi says the context best fits original disbelief: 'what preceded' means what was done while originally disbelieving, and Islam erases that, as in the report from Amr ibn al-As in Muslim that Islam, emigration, and pilgrimage erase what came before.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r17.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن الوجه في الآية هو المطابق لمقتضى المقام وأن المتبادر من الكفر الكفر الأصلي

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r18.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r18.claim: In a report in Muslim, Amr ibn al-As asks the Prophet to stipulate forgiveness at his pledge; the Prophet replies that Islam erases what came before, as do emigration and pilgrimage.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r18.anchor: أخرجه مسلم عن عمرو بن العاص قال : أتيت النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r19.claim: Al-Alusi cautions that 'what' in the hadith cannot mean absolutely everything in each of its three clauses.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r19.anchor: والظاهر أن ( ما ) لا يمكن حملها في الكل على العموم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r20.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r20.claim: Some say a convert must also repent and regret past acts, alongside faith, in order to be forgiven; al-Alusi expresses reservation about this qualification.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p206#2/r20.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن الكافر إذا أسلم يلزمه التوبة والندم على ما سلف مع الإيمان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356#2/r1.claim: If disbelievers cease from associating partners with God, their sins before Islam are forgiven.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356#2/r1.anchor: {قل للذين كفروا إن ينتهوا} عن الشرك {يغفر لهم ما قد سلف} أي: ما مضى من ذنوبهم قبل الإسلام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356#2/r2.claim: If they return to disbelief, God’s established practice of aiding His prophets and destroying their enemies applies.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356#2/r2.anchor: {وإن يعودوا فقد مضت سنة الأولين} في نصر الله أنبياءه وإهلاك أعدائه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356#2/r3.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ الرازي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356#2/r3.claim: Yahya ibn Muadh says monotheism erased prior disbelief, and he hopes it can likewise erase later sins.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p356#2/r3.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ الرازي: توحيد لم يعجز عن هدم ما قبله من كفر، أرجو أن لا يعجز عن هدم ما بعده من ذنب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r1.claim: The addressees are Abū Sufyān and his companions; “say to them” means “say for their sake.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r1.anchor: يعني أبا سفيان وأصحابه والمعنى قل لأجلهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r2.claim: If they stop opposing the Messenger by entering Islam, their past sins will be forgiven.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r2.anchor: عن معاداة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بالدخول في الإسلام

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r3.claim: Variants with tāʾ and kāf address the unbelievers directly; another reads an active verb with God as its subject.

BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r4.claim: If they return to fighting, expect the precedent of earlier groups who united against prophets and were destroyed, as at Badr.
BAYDAWI-FULL:8:38-39/r4.anchor: كما جرى على أهل بدر فليتوقعوا مثل ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r1.speaker: مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r1.claim: Malik says a convert is not held accountable for deeds committed while an unbeliever.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r1.anchor: قال مالك : لا يؤخذ كافر بشيء صنعه في كفره اذا اسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r2.speaker: مالك بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r2.claim: Malik says divorces pronounced by polytheists before conversion do not count if the parties marry after accepting Islam.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r2.anchor: قال مالك ابن انس في طلاق المشركين نساءهم ثم يتناكحون بعد اسلامهم قال : لا يعد طلاقهم شيئا

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r3.speaker: أبوه
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r3.claim: Yahya ibn Abbad's father takes their return to mean returning to fight the Muslims.

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r4.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r4.claim: Abu Malik explains مضت as خلت, meaning that it has passed.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r4.anchor: عن السدى عن أبي مالك قوله : مضت يعني : خلت

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies the precedent with Quraysh and others at Badr, as well as earlier nations.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قوله : فقد مضت سنة الاولين في قريش وغيرها يوم بدر والامم قبل ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r6.speaker: سفيان
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r6.claim: Sufyan applies the precedent to the people of Badr and their likes.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1700/r6.anchor: قال سفيان في قوله : قل للذين كفروا ان ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف وان يعودوا فقد مضت سنت الاولين في اهل بدر وامثالنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r1.claim: The Qurʾan often follows warning with encouragement or a promise, here reminding disbelievers that they can repair their past and opening the door to repentance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r1.anchor: جرى هذا الكلام على عادة القرآن في تعقيب الترهيب بالترغيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r2.claim: The sentence can answer an implicit question raised by the prior threats: whether any escape remains; the Prophet is told to announce that repentance and cessation are still possible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r2.anchor: والجملة استيناف يصح جعله بيانيا لأن ما تقدم بين يديه من الوعيد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r3.claim: The reported wording uses third person because it recounts the sense while retaining the commanded audience’s perspective, making the Prophet an informed witness rather than a mere transmitter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r3.anchor: وأسند الفعل في الجملة المحكية بالقول إلى ضمير الغائبين لأنه حكاية بالمعنى روعي فيها جانب المخاطب بالأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r4.claim: ‘Cease’ means stop the conduct signaled by their unbelief and prior effects, especially spending to obstruct God’s path; ultimately this requires faith, and the rule extends to every disbeliever.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r4.anchor: الانتهاء عن شيء معلوم دل عليه وصف الكفر هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r5.claim: ‘What has passed’ means their earlier unbelief and its consequences; forgiveness primarily means removal of afterlife punishment, and the following clause also includes worldly punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r5.anchor: هو ما أسلفوه من الكفر وآثاره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r6.claim: The verse raises legal questions about whether conversion before accountability erases liabilities incurred while a person was an unbeliever; the following discussion reports juristic answers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p343#2/r6.anchor: واستنبط أيمتنا من هذه الآية أحكاما للأفعال والتبعات التي قد تصدر من الكافر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r1.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r1.claim: Ibn al-Qāsim, Ashhab, and Ibn Wahb report from Mālik that a divorce or oath made during polytheism carries no effect after conversion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r1.anchor: روى ابن العربي في ( الأحكام ) أن ابن القاسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r2.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r2.claim: Mālik is also reported to say that ‘what has passed’ means property, blood, or other matters accrued before Islam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r2.anchor: وروى عن مالك : إنما يعني عز وجل ما قد مضى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r3.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī prefers the broad reading, citing the verse’s general wording about forgiveness of what came before.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r3.anchor: قال ابن العربي وهو الصواب لعموم قوله :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r4.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r4.claim: Mālik is reported to distinguish human claims from God’s rights: slander or theft remains punishable after conversion, while the stated penalties for adultery or raping a Muslim woman fall away.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r4.anchor: رويا عن مالك أن الكافر إذا افترى على مسلم أو سرق ثم أسلم يقام عليه الحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r5.speaker: ابن المنذر عن الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r5.claim: Al-Qurṭubī reports from Ibn al-Mundhir a similar position from al-Shāfiʿī, who argued from this verse; al-Mudawwana says all legal penalties lapse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r5.anchor: وذكر القرطبي عن ابن المنذر : أنه حكى مثل ذلك عن الشافعي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r6.claim: Al-Kashshāf attributes to Abū Ḥanīfa that a convert from the enemy camp retains no liability, while a dhimmī need not make up God’s rights but remains liable for human claims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r6.anchor: وذكر في ( الكشاف ) عن أبي حنيفة أن الحربي إذا أسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r7.speaker: علماء الحنفية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r7.claim: Hanafi legal works preserve some disagreement; they report that a repentant apostate need not make up missed prayers or pay for past crimes and damage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r7.anchor: وفي كتب الفتوى لعلماء الحنفية بعض مخالفة لهذا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r8.speaker: الشافعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r8.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī is also reported to retain all such liabilities, contrary to Ibn al-Mundhir’s attribution; Abū Ḥanīfa drops God’s rights but not people’s rights, and both use the verse with further specifications.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r8.anchor: وعن الشافعي يلزم ذلك كله وهو ما نسبه ابن العربي إلى الشافعي بخلاف ما نسبه إليه ابن المنذر كما تقدم وعن أبي حنيفة يسقط عنه كل حق هو لله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r9.claim: The phrase has a metrical embellishment: it scans in rajaz meter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r9.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى : { إن ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف } محسن بديعي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r10.claim: The two conditions contrast cessation with renewed war preparations, not unbelief after conversion; the Arabs’ ‘Islam or war?’ illustrates the contrast.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r10.anchor: لأن مقابلته بقوله : { إن ينتهوا } تقتضي أنه ترديد بين حالتين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r11.claim: ‘Return’ means renewed opposition to the Messenger and Muslims and preparation for war, as at Badr, not return to unbelief after conversion; they had not left unbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p345/r11.anchor: والمراد بالعود الرجوع إلى ما هم فيه من مناوأة الرسول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r1.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r1.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Abū Sufyān and his companions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r1.anchor: نزلت في أبي سفيان وأصحابه قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r2.claim: One reading takes the cessation to mean ending hostilities; past fighting is then forgiven and not held against them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r2.anchor: أحدهما إن ينتهوا عن المحاربة يغفر لهم ما قد سلف من حربهم فلا يؤاخذون به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r3.claim: On the war reading, returning to battle brings the established divine practice of granting victory to God's allies.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r3.anchor: وإن يعودوا إلى المحاربة فقد مضت سنة الأولين في نصر الله أولياءه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r4.claim: An alternative explains the earlier practice as the killing of some and capture of others at Badr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r4.anchor: وقيل في قتل من قتل يوم بدر وأسر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r5.claim: A second reading takes cessation to mean abandoning unbelief, which brings forgiveness for earlier sins.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r5.anchor: والثاني إن ينتهوا عن الكفر يغفر لهم ما قد سلف من الإثم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r6.claim: If they return to unbelief, the precedent is the annihilating punishment that overtook earlier nations.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r6.anchor: فقد مضت سنة الأولين من الأمم السالفة حين أخذوا بالعذاب المستأصل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r7.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r7.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh says that if monotheism can erase prior unbelief, it can also erase sins committed afterward.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p356#2/r7.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ في هذه الآية إن توحيدا لم يعجز عن هدم ما قبله من كفر

JISHUMI:v4p2926/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r3.claim: Intihāʾ means stopping because of a prohibition: one forbids something, and the person desists.
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r3.anchor: الانتهاء: الإقلاع لأجل النهي، يقال: نهاه عن كذا فانتهى.

JISHUMI:v4p2926/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r4.claim: Sunna means a path or conduct; the cited poetic line illustrates a path one has established, and the term can also mean an action maintained for a long time, including prophetic practice.
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r4.anchor: والسنة: الطريقة والسيرة، قال الشاعر: ولا تجزعن من سنة أنت سرتها

JISHUMI:v4p2926/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r5.claim: Sulūf means going ahead or preceding; salafa and aslafa are related forms.
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r5.anchor: والسلوف: التقديم، سلف يسلف سلوفا وأسلف إسلافا.

JISHUMI:v4p2926/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r8.claim: One report says the verse was revealed concerning Abu Sufyan and his companions; another says its address is general.
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r8.anchor: قيل: نزلت الآية في أبي [سفيان وأصحابه]. وقيل: هو عام.

JISHUMI:v4p2926/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r9.claim: After the preceding promise and threat, the verse invites repentance and faith.
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r9.anchor: لما تقدم الوعد والوعيد عقبه بالدعاء إلى التوبة والإيمان، فقال سبحانه: قل يا محمد

JISHUMI:v4p2926/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r10.claim: If the disbelievers desist, they repent of their present idolatry and refrain from it.
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r10.anchor: إن ينتهوا يتوبوا عما هم عليه من الشرك ويمتنعوا،

JISHUMI:v4p2926/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r11.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r11.claim: Al-Asamm specifies that they must desist from idolatry and fighting the believers.
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r11.anchor: وقيل: عن الشرك وقتال المؤمنين، عن الأصم.

JISHUMI:v4p2926/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r12.claim: What is forgiven is their prior unbelief, fighting the Prophet, and persecuting believers: they incur no worldly retaliation or liability and no punishment for these in the afterlife.
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r12.anchor: مضى منهم من الكفر وقتال النبي، وإفتان المؤمنين عن دينهم يغفر لهم ذلك في أحكام الدنيا، فلا يؤاخذون بقصاص وضمان،

JISHUMI:v4p2926/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r13.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r13.claim: If they return to unbelief and fighting Muslims, the precedent of earlier peoples has already occurred.
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r13.anchor: وإن يعودوا قيل: إلى الكفر وقتال المسلمين فقد مضت سنت الأولين

JISHUMI:v4p2926/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r14.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r14.claim: Abu Muslim explains the precedent as God’s support of prophets, destruction of disbelievers in this world, and punishment in the next, as at Badr.
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r14.anchor: يعني طريقته في نصرة الأنبياء، والإهلاك للكفار في الدنيا، وبالعذاب في الآخرة كما فعل يوم بدر، عن أبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v4p2926/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r15.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد والسدي
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r15.claim: Al-Hasan, Mujahid, and al-Suddi explain it as prompt annihilating punishment and its like, including captivity and killing at Badr.
JISHUMI:v4p2926/r15.anchor: وقيل: بتعجيل عذاب الاستئصال، وما جرى مجراه من الأسر والقتل يوم بدر، عن الحسن ومجاهد والسدي.

JISHUMI:v1p792/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p792/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p792/r1.claim: If the disbelievers desist, they have stopped their unbelief through repentance; God covers their sins and rewards them in paradise.
JISHUMI:v1p792/r1.anchor: فإن انتهوا امتنعوا عن كفرهم بالتوبة فإن الله غفور رحيم

JISHUMI:v1p792/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p792/r2.speaker: unspecified
JISHUMI:v1p792/r2.claim: An alternative supplies omitted words: if they desist by repenting, God forgives them because He is forgiving and merciful.
JISHUMI:v1p792/r2.anchor: وقيل: فيه حذف، وتقديره: فإن انتهوا بالتوبة، فإن الله يغفر لهم

JISHUMI:v1p792/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p792/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p792/r3.claim: Fighting is obligatory only while they persist in unbelief and is forbidden once they desist.
JISHUMI:v1p792/r3.anchor: تدل الآية على أن قتالهم يجب بشرط إقامتهم على الكفر، وأنه محظور إذا انتهوا

JISHUMI:v1p792/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p792/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p792/r4.claim: The verse establishes that repentance is accepted from every sin, including the greatest sin of unbelief, refuting the claim that a murderer cannot repent.
JISHUMI:v1p792/r4.anchor: وتدل على أن التوبة مقبولة من كل ذنب؛ لأن الكفر أعظم الذنوب، فيبطل قول من يقول

JISHUMI:v1p792/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p792/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p792/r5.claim: The verse refutes the claim that a repentant person needs no forgiveness and only a persistent sinner needs it, since forgiveness follows their desistance.
JISHUMI:v1p792/r5.anchor: وتدل على بطلان القول بأن التائب لا يحتاج إلى مغفرة، وإنما يحتاج إليها المصر

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r1.claim: One reading is that they cease hostilities and make peace, so previous liability and punishment are forgiven.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r1.anchor: إن ينتهوا عن المحاربة إلى الموادعة يغفر لهم ما قد سلف من المؤاخذة والمعاقبة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r2.claim: Another reading is that they cease disbelief by embracing Islam, so their previous sins are forgiven.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r2.anchor: إن ينتهوا عن الكفر بالإسلام يغفر لهم ما قد سلف من الآثام

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r3.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r3.claim: If they return to fighting, the precedent is Badr, where some were killed and others taken captive.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r3.anchor: وإن يعودوا إلى المحاربة فقد مضت سنة الأولين فيمن قتل يوم بدر وأسر , قاله الحسن ومجاهد والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r4.claim: If they return to disbelief, the precedent is the destruction God inflicted on earlier nations in this world.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r4.anchor: فقد مضت سنة الأولين من الأمم السالفة فيما أخذهم الله به في الدنيا من عذاب الاستئصال

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r5.claim: After Mecca’s conquest, the Prophet asked its people what they expected him to do; they appealed to his generosity, and he answered with Joseph’s words before this verse was revealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p318/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس : نزلت هذه الآية في أهل مكة بعد أن دخلها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عام الفتح

MUJAHID:v1p262#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p262#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p262#3/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies those who return to disbelief as Quraysh at Badr and earlier peoples who had met the established fate.
MUJAHID:v1p262#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ وإن يعودوا فقد مضت سنة الأولين ﴾ يعني قريش يوم بدر وفي غيرها من الأمم قبل ذلك

MUQATIL:8:38-40/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:8:38-40/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:8:38-40/r1.claim: If unbelievers stop associating partners with God and repent, their pre-Islamic acts of associating partners are forgiven.
MUQATIL:8:38-40/r1.anchor: عن الشرك ويتوبوا، { يغفر لهم ما قد سلف } من شركهم قبل الإسلام

MUQATIL:8:38-40/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:8:38-40/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:8:38-40/r2.claim: If they return to fighting the Prophet without repenting, the precedent of earlier peoples is their killing at Badr; the warning is meant to prevent another such return.
MUQATIL:8:38-40/r2.anchor: لقتال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ولم يتوبوا، { فقد مضت سنة الأولين } [آية: 38]، يعني القتل ببدر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r1.claim: The disbelievers addressed are Abū Sufyān and his companions.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r2.claim: They must stop hostility and fighting against the Messenger by entering Islam.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r2.anchor: عماهم عليه من عداوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقتلاه بالدخول فى الإسلام

NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r3.claim: If they stop, their past hostility will be forgiven.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r4.claim: If they resume fighting, earlier peoples’ destruction and punishment will apply in this world and the next.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r4.anchor: بالإهلاك فى الدنيا والعذاب قفى العقى ب أو معناه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r5.claim: Alternatively, stopping means abandoning disbelief and becoming Muslim, in which case prior disbelief and sins are forgiven.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r5.anchor: أن الكفار إذا انتهوع عن الكفر وأسلموا غفرلهم ماقد سلف

NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r6.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa cites this verse to argue that an apostate who returns to Islam need not make up worship missed while apostate.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p65/r6.anchor: وبه احتج أبو حنيفة رحمه الله فى أن المرتد إذا أسلم لم يلزمه قضاء العبادات المتروكة

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r1.claim: The Prophet must convey this meaning to the disbelievers, in these words or another phrasing.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r1.anchor: أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يقول للكفار هذا المعنى، وسواء قاله بهذه العبارة أو غيرها

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah discusses al-Kisāʾī’s report that Ibn Masʿūd’s codex reads “if they cease”; on that wording the message would depend on those exact words.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ولو كان كما ذكر الكسائي أنه في مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah says “if they desist” means desisting from disbelief, as the conditional answer promises forgiveness for what came before.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r3.anchor: يريد عن الكفر. قال ابن عطية: ولا بد والحامل على ذلك جواب الشرط

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد أحمد بن محمد الزبيري
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r4.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Zubayrī’s verse says that confessing and stopping wrongdoing merits pardon.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r4.anchor: ولقد أحسن القائل أبو سعيد أحمد بن محمد الزبيري

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r5.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r5.claim: Muslim reports Abū Shumāsah al-Muḥāribī visiting the dying ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, who recalls the Prophet saying Islam, emigration, and pilgrimage each efface what came before.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r5.anchor: روى مسلم عن أبي شماسة المهري قال: حضرنا عمرو بن العاص

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r6.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r6.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī calls the pardon divine kindness: wiping away prior sins makes repentance and conversion easier, since fear would deter people from returning to Islam.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r6.anchor: قال ابن العربي: هذه لطيفة من الله سبحانه من بها على الخلق

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r7.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r7.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī warns that deterring repentance harms people, while easing the way to mercy benefits them.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r7.anchor: فالتنفير مفسدة للخليقة، والتيسير مصلحة لهم

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r8.claim: A Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim report tells of a man who killed ninety-nine people, was told by an ascetic he had no repentance, killed him too, and reached one hundred; despair drove him to kill.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r8.anchor: لا توبة لك فقتله فكمل به مائة

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly told a would-be killer there was no repentance to deter him, but assured an actual killer of repentance to draw him toward it.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r9.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه كان إذا جاء إليه رجل لم يقتل

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r10.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r10.claim: Mālik, transmitted by Ibn al-Qāsim and Ibn Wahb, says pre-Islamic divorce and oaths lapse on conversion, but a convert remains liable for slandering or stealing from a Muslim.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38/r10.anchor: قال ابن القاسم وابن وهب عن مالك فيمن طلق في الشرك ثم أسلم فلا طلاق له

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r1.claim: Ashhab transmits Mālik limiting pardon to pre-Islamic matters, including property and blood claims.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r1.anchor: وروى أشهب عن مالك أنه قال: إنما يعني الله عز وجل ما قد مضى قبل الإسلام

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī considers the broad pardon correct, given the verse’s general wording, the report that Islam erases what preceded it, and the benefit of easing conversion.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وهذا هو الصواب لما قدمناه من عموم قوله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r3.speaker: author
