QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r3.claim: Combatant disbelievers’ offenses in enemy territory are forgiven; safe-conduct visitors and dhimmīs retain penalties for slander, theft, and murder because the covenant was breached.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r3.anchor: أما الكافر الحربي فلا خلاف في إسقاط ما فعله في حال كفره

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r4.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī in Iraq held that a Christian who committed adultery then converted is not flogged or banished; Ibn al-Mundhir says this agrees with what is reported from Mālik.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r4.anchor: عن الشافعي رضي الله عنه إذ هو بالعراق لا حد عليه ولا تغريب

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r5.speaker: أبو ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r5.claim: Abū Thawr says a convert who admits while Muslim that he committed adultery as a Christian receives the penalty.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r5.anchor: وقال أبو ثور: إذا أقر وهو مسلم أنه زنى وهو كافر أقيم عليه الحد

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r6.speaker: الكوفي
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r6.claim: The Kūfan authority disagrees with Abū Thawr and says the convert is not punished for that adultery.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r6.anchor: وحكي عن الكوفي أنه قال: لا يحد

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r7.claim: One view treats a returning apostate like an original disbeliever who converts, imposing no liability for missed prayers, offenses, or destroyed property during apostasy.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r7.anchor: فقيل: حكمه حكم الكافر الأصلي إذا أسلم لا يؤخذ بشيء مما أحدثه في حال ارتداده

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r8.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r8.claim: In one opinion al-Shāfiʿī makes a returning apostate liable for all rights of God and people, reasoning that if human rights remain, divine rights should too.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r8.anchor: وقال الشافعي في أحد قوليه: يلزمه كل حق لله عز وجل وللآدمي

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r9.claim: Abū Ḥanīfah says rights owed to God lapse for a returning apostate, but rights owed to people remain.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r9.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: ما كان لله يسقط، وما كان للآدمي لا يسقط

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r10.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r10.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī endorses the Ḥanafī view: God does not need His due, people do; children likewise owe no divine duties but remain subject to human claims.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r10.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وهو قول علمائنا لأن الله تعالى مستغن عن حقه

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r11.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r11.claim: The verse’s promise is also cited as general for rights owed to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r11.anchor: قالوا: وقوله تعالى { قل للذين كفروا إن ينتهوا يغفر لهم ما قد سلف } عام في الحقوق لله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r12.claim: “If they return” means return to fighting: the unqualified ʿāda denotes returning to a prior state, and disbelievers had not left disbelief.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r12.anchor: الخامسة: قوله تعالى: { وإن يعودوا } يريد إلى القتال

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r13.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah says fighting is the only prior state they could return to, not disbelief, which they never abandoned.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r13.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ولسنا نجد في هذه الآية لهؤلاء الكفار حالة تشبه ما ذكرنا إلا القتال

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r14.claim: Arabic ʿāda can mean “became” when followed by a predicate, as in ʿāda Zaydun malikan; this does not imply return to an earlier state.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r14.anchor: لأنها قد تجيء في كلام العرب داخلة في الابتداء والخبر، فيكون معناها معنى صار

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r15.claim: Umayyah ibn Abī al-Ṣalt’s cited line illustrates ʿāda meaning “became,” not “returned,” because the verb is restricted by its predicate.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#2/r15.anchor: ومنه قول أمية بن أبي الصلت

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#3/r1.claim: Umayyah’s poetic line about bowls of milk mixed with water that became urine witnesses ʿāda in the sense “became.”
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#3/r1.anchor: تلك المكارم لا قعبان من لبن شيبا بماء فعادا بعد أبوالا

QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#3/r2.claim: The former peoples’ precedent combines warning and threat with examples of nations destroyed by God’s punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:8:38#3/r2.anchor: عبارة تجمع الوعيد والتهديد والتمثيل بمن هلك من الأمم في سالف الدهر بعذاب الله

RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r1.claim: The Kashshāf explains “say to those who disbelieve” as “say on their behalf this statement”; if it meant addressing them directly, the wording would be “if you desist.”
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : { قل للذين كفروا } أي قل لأجلهم هذا القول

RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd is cited for the direct-address wording “if you desist,” supporting the alternative parsing.

RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r3.claim: If unbelievers abandon disbelief and hostility to the Messenger, enter Islam, and accept its law, God forgives their past disbelief and hostility.
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r3.anchor: الكفر وعداوة الرسول ، ودخلوا الإسلام والتزموا شرائعه

RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r4.claim: If they return to disbelief and persist, the precedents of earlier peoples apply to them.
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r4.anchor: وإن عادوا إليه وإصروا عليه فقد مضت سنة الأولين

RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r5.claim: One interpretation is that the precedent refers to the earlier unbelievers whose plot recoiled upon them at Badr.
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r5.anchor: المراد فقد مضت سنة الأولين منهم الذين حاق بهم مكرهم يوم بدر

RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r6.claim: A second interpretation refers to past nations that united against their prophets; the present unbelievers should expect the same fate if they do not desist.
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r6.anchor: فقد مضت سنة الأولين الذين تحزبوا على أنبيائهم من الأمم الذين قد مروا

RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r7.claim: A third interpretation identifies the precedent with God’s promises that His messengers will prevail and the righteous will inherit the earth.
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r7.anchor: وهي قوله : { كتب الله لاغلبن أنا ورسلى }

RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r8.claim: Rāzī holds that repentance by a zindīq is accepted; the verse’s promise of forgiveness to those who desist from disbelief covers every kind of unbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r8.anchor: والصحيح أنها مقبولة لوجوه : الأول : هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r9.claim: Although one may not know inwardly whether a zindīq has abandoned the heresy, legal judgments rest on appearances; once the person returns, the profession of repentance is accepted.
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r9.anchor: أحكام الشرع مبنية على الظواهر ، كما قال عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r10.claim: A person is obligated to repent and has no route to repentance except this act; refusing to accept it would impose an impossible duty.
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r10.anchor: لا شك أنه مكلف بالرجوع ولا طريق له إليه إلا بهذه التوبة فلو لم تقبل لزم تكليف ما لا يطاق

RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r11.claim: Rāzī also supports acceptance of repentance with the verse stating that God accepts repentance from His servants and pardons sins.
RAZI-FULL:v15p130/r11.anchor: وهو الذى يقبل التوبة عن عباده ويعفوا عن السيئات
